question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: 1,000 × sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by eligible crash-row count, by crash year
options.denominator: eligible police-reported crash rows for that year (all have a nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed value)
options.reason: Deaths per reported crash normalize annual motorist-death counts by crash volume while retaining multiple deaths from the same crash.
options.answer: This file cannot establish whether motorist-death risk per mile declined; it shows 0.540 motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crash rows in 2013 and 0.947 in 2025, with a 2023 peak of 1.273.
options.interpretation: The data cannot determine whether motorist-death risk per mile declined; this option shows 0.540 motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crash rows in 2013 and 0.947 in 2025, with a peak of 1.273 in 2023. The metric sums number_of_motorist_killed and divides by one row per police-reported NYC crash, a defensible crash-normalized fatality-burden measure that still does not account for miles driven. The population is all NYC reported motor vehicle crashes in full calendar years 2013–2025; the check found 0 missing crash dates and 0 missing motorist-death values in every year, so no in-scope rows were dropped for these fields. The denominator rose from 203,742 rows in 2013 to 231,564 in 2018, then reached 85,546 in 2025; comparisons are per recorded crash and do not adjust for annual driving exposure.
